sourcedFrom: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. (ABSENT — no copyright line printed.)
cleanIntro: A modular .30 can that changes length is a can with more threads and more indexing than most, and both of those are what a cleaning schedule protects. Silencer Central puts the interval at 50 to 100 rounds and prints an end-cap torque — this is one of the few cans whose own book gives you a number to tighten to.

steps.title: Host unloaded and open, and the can off it
steps.action: Nothing starts until the action is open and you have looked into it. Then the can comes off — and it comes off hot for far longer than it looks.
steps.aside: When removing the silencer, use extreme caution as it may be hot to the touch after firing.
steps.quote: Before removing the silencer from the host firearm, be sure that the firearm is unloaded, and the action is opened so that it is visibly clear of any ammunition.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — WARNING, printed p.2-3

steps.title: End cap off with the key and a T-45
steps.action: Both tools, together — the tool key and the T-45. The book's own tip is to bond the two into one tool so the pair is never half-missing when the can needs opening at the bench.
steps.aside: It is recommended that the suppressor be cleaned every 50 - 100 rounds fired.
steps.quote: To disassemble make sure the firearm is unloaded and remove from host firearm.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLE, printed p.8

steps.title: ⛔ Front module off — and the barrel-side cap stays put
steps.action: The front module unthreads from the main tube; that is the joint that opens. ⛔ The cap at the barrel end is not one of them, and the book says so in as many words. Turning it is how a tube gets damaged for nothing.
steps.aside: The end cap of the suppressor that threads onto the barrel is not intended to be removed from the main tube of the suppressor.
steps.quote: Remove the front module from the main tube.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLE, printed p.8

steps.title: Soak a full day before the baffles move
steps.action: Solvent inside, then leave it for twenty-four hours. A day sounds like a lot until you have tried to drive a dry .30 baffle stack out of a titanium tube; the soak is what makes the next step a push instead of a fight.
steps.aside: Push baffles out of the tube with our Baffle Removal Tool (sold separately) or a wooden dowel.
steps.quote: Using your solvent of choice, spray the inside of the suppressor and let sit for 24 hours.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLE, printed p.8

steps.title: ⛔ Count the baffles as they come out
steps.action: This can ships in two lengths with two baffle counts, and the reassembly differs between them. Lay the stack out in the order it came out and count it — that count is the only thing that tells you which configuration you are putting back.
steps.quote: The suppressor is either 6.4” or 8.2” with 8 or 11 baffles. Care must be taken when reassembling.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLE, printed p.8

steps.title: Stiff brush, brass or nylon, baffles and tube
steps.action: Work the baffle faces and the inside of the tube with solvent and a stiff brush. The indexing tabs matter as much as the faces: carbon in a tab is what stops a stack seating square, and a stack that will not seat square will not let the end cap go down.
steps.aside: The use of solid lead or plated lead bullets is not recommended.
steps.quote: Make sure all parts are clean and solvent has been removed.
steps.cite: BANISH 30-V2 OWNER'S MANUAL — ABSENT — no revision or edition statement is printed in the document; the cached file is the 2025 posting. — CLEANING & DISASSEMBLE, printed p.8

deepAbsentReason: There is nothing below this. Silencer Central publishes ONE procedure for the BANISH 30-V2 and the field strip above is all of it — cap, module, baffle stack, brush. A baffle does not itself come apart, and the one joint the book explicitly withholds (the barrel-side end cap in the main tube) is carried as a PROHIBITION rather than being quietly turned into a deeper step. ⛔ Inventing a deeper teardown for a can would be exactly the substitution the sealed/serviceable record exists to prevent.

cleaning.name: BAFFLE STACK
tasks: Soaked 24 hours in solvent before anything is pushed
Pushed out with the maker's tool or a wooden dowel — never driven
Faces AND indexing tabs brushed; a fouled tab stops the stack seating square
Counted out and laid in order — 8 or 11, and the two configurations differ

cleaning.name: TUBE AND MODULE
tasks: Inside of the main tube and the extension brushed with solvent
All solvent removed before anything goes back
⛔ The barrel-side end cap stays in the main tube

cleaning.name: THREADS
tasks: Anti-seize on the threads before the end cap or modular end goes back
Mount and barrel threads checked clean and undamaged
⛔ No gap between barrel shoulder and thread mount, ever

cleaning.name: ⛔ THE SCHEDULE IS THE MAINTENANCE
tasks: Every 50–100 rounds, by the maker's own number
Solid lead and plated lead are not recommended through this can

reassembly: Seven matching baffles stacked on a flat surface, indexing tabs aligned and fully engaged.
Tube slid over the stack, upright, and the stack pushed up until it indexes with the main tube.
Assembly flipped open-end up, and the threads get anti-seize before anything is started into them.
Short baffle into the main tube; for the long configuration, two tall extension baffles and a short one into the extension tube, then the end cap.
End cap started light — only the 45° bevel showing, about 1/32"; an o-ring in sight means the tabs are wrong.
Finish to 110–120 inch pounds, then check the bore is clear before it goes back on a barrel.
fncheck: Reassembled and off the gun: with the baffles indexed correctly ONLY the 45-degree bevel on the end cap shows, about 1/32". If more than that is proud, or you can see the o-ring, the tabs are not aligned and the cap comes back off — torquing it down at that point is how a baffle stack gets crushed. Then 110–120 inch-pounds, and a clear look down the bore.
